turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Sits down without taking off her coat and sets a folded legal pad on the desk.*

Mr. Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so you have until then. Before anything else, why was Owen's zero in the gradebook before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.

*Doesn't return the greeting. Glances at the clock on the wall.*

Thanks is not an answer. You entered the zero without calling me, which is what your own procedure says not to do. Why?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.

*Pulls the printed Turnitin guide from her bag and sets it on the desk, face up.*

A machine's guess. Your own procedure says software alone does not establish a concern, and the company that sells that checker says not to use it as the sole basis for punishing a student. Did you read that, or did you just read 94?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.

*Taps the printed page once with a finger.*

"Quite reliable." Okay. Show me the reliability studies, then. Or is "quite" the whole argument?
So I had to give him a zero.

*Writes something on the legal pad.*

"Had to." Procedure 4.3 says you didn't have to. Who told you that, and did you ask Owen a single question before you entered it?
I hope you understand my position.

*Looks up from the pad.*

I understand your position. You're the one who entered a zero on a machine's number and called me afterwards. Did you ask Owen anything before that, yes or no?
